subject: Conversation flow degradation: high latency on streaming endpoints — action items
messages:
From: Elena Moretti <elena.moretti@finpay.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinPay SRE Team <sre@finpay.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Chat sessions stalling / long tail latency since 06:00 PDT

Hi Ben —

We started seeing a spike in tail latency on your streaming/chat endpoint (conversation API) around 06:00 PDT this morning. For some users the stream appears to hang for 8–12s between token chunks; others see near-normal throughput. This is affecting our web live chat (low volume demo environment) and a couple of flows fail entirely.

I attached a quick latency graph from our client-side logs (latency_graph_20270418.png). Key observations:
- 95th percentile token latency increased from ~130ms to ~1.2s after 06:00
- Problem seems intermittent and correlated with a small number of long-lived sessions
- We tried immediate retries and exponential backoff but saw mixed results

Can you confirm if there’s an ongoing degradation on Redwood’s side and recommended short-term mitigations we can apply while you investigate? We’re prepping a customer-facing update and need clear guidance to avoid over-notifying our users.

Thanks,
Elena Moretti
Senior Product Ops — FinPay
elena.moretti@finpay.com

[attachment: latency_graph_20270418.png]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Moretti <elena.moretti@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 16:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Chat sessions stalling / long tail latency since 06:00 PDT

Elena — thanks for the quick heads up and for the graph. We’re seeing the same noisy tail in internal metrics. I’ve looped in Karthik (SRE) and Marissa (Customer Success) so we can coordinate a concise action plan.

Short-term mitigations you can try immediately (non-destructive, low-risk):
1) Switch to the non-streaming endpoint (polling) for critical flows temporarily — this avoids incremental delivery stalls and keeps the UX predictable.
2) Reduce max_tokens to limit long generations and lower token-churn.
3) Add a small client-side token timeout and retry with incremental backoff (200ms -> 500ms -> 1000ms) — prefer idempotent retries only.
4) If you’re using the latest model variant, try pinning to the -lowlatency variant (if available) or a smaller model for high-SLA channels.

We’ll:
- Run an initial postmortem within 12 hours.
- Provide a one-page customer advisory and suggested wording for your support team.
- Share any confirmed root cause and timeline for a fix.

Marissa — can you draft a short note we can share with FinPay customers describing the issue and how it impacts streaming vs non-streaming UX? Karthik — can you confirm we’re not seeing correlated infra failures (GPU OOMs, network saturation) and share the early signal for the incident ticket?

Ben Carter
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Chat sessions stalling / long tail latency since 06:00 PDT

Ben / Marissa — quick triage notes from infra:
- We observed an elevated error rate and increased service time on the streaming edge between 05:55–17:10 PDT. Not seeing GPU OOMs or node reboots.
- Early hypothesis: degraded KV cache hit rates for a small subset of long-lived sessions causing repeated re-computation and slower token emission.
- There’s also an increased queuing time on a subset of model shards during mixed-short/long sequence load.

Immediate actions taken (15–30m):
- Applied a temporary routing policy to move new streaming sessions to lower-utilization shards (best-effort).
- Enabled aggressive KV prefix eviction on affected pools to reduce cache thrash.
- Instrumented additional tracing for affected sessions (INC-7213).

Short-term recommended customer guidance (we can send as a single paragraph):

"We are investigating an intermittent increase in token latency affecting a small number of streaming sessions. Recommended temporary mitigations: switch critical flows to the non-streaming (polling) API, reduce max_tokens, and add an idempotent retry/backoff for token timeouts. We will share a follow-up with root cause and ETA for a permanent fix."

I’ll validate the routing change impact over the next 60–90m and report back. If routing brings tail latency down, we’ll roll out the policy wider.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer, Senior SRE — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Subject: Incident follow-up and customer playbook for FinPay (Incident INC-7213)

Elena —

Thanks again for surfacing this. Summary of what we found and guidance you can share with your ops team and customers:

What happened (summary)
- Intermittent increased token emission latency on streaming endpoints observed 2027-04-18 05:55–17:10 PDT.
- Root cause (confirmed): transient KV-cache thrash combined with uneven shard queuing for mixed-length session workloads; a small fraction of long-lived sessions amplified tail latency.

What we changed (short-term / corrective)
- Applied routing policy to move new streaming sessions away from affected shards (reduced incidence by ~70% in our canary).
- Enabled aggressive KV prefix eviction to reduce cache collision windows.
- Added tracing and retention for affected sessions to support postmortem.

Customer-facing mitigations you can use now
- For critical flows where predictability matters, use the non-streaming (polling) endpoint until we confirm full remediation.
- Reduce max_tokens to shorten response windows and lower token churn.
- Implement client-side token timeouts + idempotent retries with exponential backoff (recommended backoff windows: 200ms, 500ms, 1000ms).
- Consider pinning to a -lowlatency model variant for high-SLA channels if available in your catalog.

Next steps and timeline
- We will circulate a full incident postmortem by 2027-04-21. That will include a permanent mitigation plan: improved shard balancing, KV cache isolation per customer pool, and a targeted scheduler change to prioritize streaming token emission.
- We are offering a one-time usage credit for impacted requests while the remediation rolls out; I’ll connect you to our billing specialist if you want to accept.

Attachments included: latency_graph_20270418.png (your original), proposed_mitigation_steps.docx (playbook + suggested customer messaging).

Marissa will follow up with a succinct customer advisory copy you can paste into support notices; Karthik will update once the routing change is fully rolled out.

Please let me know if you want us to send a joint customer notice from Redwood + FinPay.
